evals.prompt: Audit tpir-scen-2 in skills/audit-tpir-boundary/evals/fixtures/candidate-tpir-inventories.json for FedRAMP Class D compliance.
evals.expected_output: tpir-scen-2 fails Class D residency mandatory gates (BLOCKING): although it cites a certified package ID and FIPS 140-3 mTLS, setting us_jurisdiction_only=false and configuring automatic disaster-recovery failover to Toronto, Canada violates CTL.SA.SA-09-05 (Class D MUST restrict all information processing, federal customer data, and system services to U.S./U.S. Territories or geographic locations under U.S. jurisdiction). Failover routes on Class D MUST remain strictly within U.S. jurisdiction and fail closed rather than crossing outside U.S. jurisdiction. Grounding: pinned to skills/audit-tpir-boundary/evals/fixtures/candidate-tpir-inventories.json.
expectations: Identifies the Toronto, Canada failover route and us_jurisdiction_only=false as a BLOCKING Class D violation of CTL.SA.SA-09-05
Explains that even a certified cloud provider or DR failover path cannot process Class D Federal Customer Data outside U.S./U.S. Territories/U.S. jurisdiction
Requires fail-closed U.S.-jurisdiction-only failover routing with us_jurisdiction_only=true

evals.prompt: Consult the live schemas/tpir-register.schema.json and templates/agent-manifest.example.class-c.json in this repository: what fields are required to document a non-certified CI/CD delivery pipeline TPIR properly, and what boundary controls keep it compliant?
evals.expected_output: Live-corpus check: In schemas/tpir-register.schema.json (under thirdPartyInformationResources.nonCertified[]), every non-certified TPIR requires nine fields: name, provider, website, useCase, generalUsageAndConfiguration, justification, mitigationMeasures (non-empty array), and compensatingControls (non-empty array) — and in agent-manifest.json tpirs[], it requires name, certified=false, fedramp_package_id=null, use_case, and non-empty mitigations. As demonstrated in templates/agent-manifest.example.class-c.json, a non-certified CI/CD delivery pipeline stays compliant under MAS-CSO-TPR and KSI-SCR-MIT only when zero Federal Customer Data or runtime prompts enter the build plane, builds run on ephemeral self-hosted runners inside the CSO boundary with federated short-lived credentials, and artifacts enforce cryptographic digest pinning and provenance signatures (CTL.CM.CM-14, CTL.SR.SR-03). Grounding: live lookup against schemas/tpir-register.schema.json and templates/agent-manifest.example.class-c.json.
expectations: Reads live schemas/tpir-register.schema.json and enumerates the required nonCertified object fields (name, provider, website, useCase, generalUsageAndConfiguration, justification, mitigationMeasures, compensatingControls)
Notes certified=false and fedramp_package_id=null in agent-manifest.json tpirs[]

States the core boundary controls from templates/agent-manifest.example.class-c.json (zero Federal Customer Data in build plane, ephemeral in-boundary runners, cryptographic digest/signature verification)
